name: Missing Initialization of Resource
principle: The product fails to initialize a critical resource before it can affect behavior. The resource may contain stale, unpredictable, or unsafe default data, causing data exposure, privilege mistakes, crashes, or later use of an uninitialized resource.
detection_signals: C/C++ local variable declared without initializer and later read: `int uid; ... if (uid == 0)`
C/C++ local pointer declared without initializer and later dereferenced or passed to `%s`: `char *p; printf("%s", p)`
C buffer used with string APIs before null initialization: `char buf[N]; strcat(buf, src)`
Variable assigned only inside `if`/`try`/`switch` branch and used after branch without `else`/`default` assignment
Security state variable assigned only after external call success: `state = getState(); if (state) uid = parse(state); if (uid == 0)`
Initialization guard starts in completed state: `private boolean initialized = true; if (!initialized) init()`
Reused buffer or struct sent with `send`/`write`/serialization without prior `memset`, constructor, or field initialization
negative_signals: Declaration includes safe initializer: `int uid = -1;`, `char buf[20] = "";`, `char *p = NULL;`
All control-flow branches assign the resource before use, including `else` or `default`
Failure path returns, throws, or aborts before the uninitialized value can be used
C++ object fields are initialized in constructor member-initializer list before any method use
Java field or object state is explicitly set to a safe value in constructor before security checks
Buffer is cleared or initialized before output: `memset(buf, 0, sizeof buf)` or `buf[0] = '\0'`
false_defense_traps: Assuming stack or heap memory starts as zero in C/C++
Checking only the success branch of a conditional initialization
Using `strcat` on a fixed-size buffer without first making it an empty string
Relying on a default value that is privileged, such as `uid == 0`
Setting an `initialized` flag before all initialization steps complete
verification_focus: Can any execution path reach a read, security decision, output, or API use of the resource before it is explicitly initialized to a safe value?

consequence_chains.trigger: Resource is not initialized and is later consumed
consequence_chains.consequence: Unpredictable control flow, crash, or incorrect security decision

consequence_chains.trigger: Uninitialized string buffer lacks a null terminator before string API use
consequence_chains.consequence: Out-of-bounds read, information disclosure, or crash

consequence_chains.trigger: Concurrent initialization exposes a partially initialized resource
consequence_chains.consequence: Other thread observes unsafe state or skips required initialization

patch_principle: Explicitly initialize every critical resource before first use.
Give security-sensitive state a fail-closed default such as deny, invalid, or least privilege.
Ensure every conditional, error, `catch`, `else`, and `default` path initializes or exits before use.
Follow the complete required API initialization sequence before using the resource.
Enable compiler/static-analysis warnings for uninitialized variables, such as `-Wuninitialized` and `-Wmaybe-uninitialized`.
